title: Docker Reference
description: A quick reminder of the ideas and examples in the Docker lessons. Open the linked lesson when you need more help.

entries.name: Images and containers
entries.summary: An image is a packaged starting point. A container is a running or stopped instance created from an image.
notes: Installing a command-line client alone does not mean the Docker engine is running.

entries.name: Run a small example
entries.summary: docker run creates and starts a container. --rm asks Docker to remove that container after it exits.
notes: --rm removes the container after exit; it does not delete the image.

entries.name: See local images
entries.summary: An image list shows packages stored on your machine. A tag is a readable label for an image version.
notes: A mutable tag can later point to another image; it is not a permanent content identity.

entries.name: List containers
entries.summary: docker ps lists running containers. Adding -a also shows stopped containers that were not automatically removed.
notes: A stopped container and a deleted container are different states.

entries.name: Name a practice container
entries.summary: A container name gives you a clear target for later inspection. The -d option runs it in the background.
notes: Use a fresh name and bind practice ports to 127.0.0.1 so they are not exposed on every network interface.

entries.name: Read container logs
entries.summary: Logs record messages written by a container's program. They help explain what it is doing or why it stopped.
notes: Do not put secrets into logs; logs are often copied elsewhere.

entries.name: Inspect container details
entries.summary: inspect returns detailed configuration and state. A format expression can select a small part of the result.
notes: Inspect only containers you own or have permission to examine.

entries.name: Read a Dockerfile
entries.summary: A Dockerfile describes how to build an image. FROM chooses a base; COPY adds a file from the build folder.
notes: Do not COPY secret files into an image; image layers can retain them.

entries.name: Build a local image
entries.summary: docker build reads a Dockerfile and its build context. -t gives the resulting image a tag.
notes: A large or secret-filled build context can include files you did not intend to send to the builder.

entries.name: Keep unwanted files out
entries.summary: A .dockerignore file excludes matching files from the build context. This keeps temporary or private files out of a build.
notes: Ignoring a file in Git and ignoring it in a Docker build are separate settings.

entries.name: Volumes store data outside a container
entries.summary: A volume is storage managed separately from a container's writable layer. It can outlive a particular container.

example.code:
Container A writes a note to a named volume
Container A is removed
Container B mounts the same volume and reads the note

notes: A volume is not automatically a backup and is not deleted by removing only the container.

entries.name: Stop and remove only your practice container
entries.summary: Cleanup should target the exact resource you created. Stopping a container is separate from removing it.

example.code:
docker stop club-web
docker rm club-web

notes: Do not use broad prune commands on a shared machine while learning.
